title: Consumer impact snapshot and self-serve recovery kit
short_summary: Brief customer-facing snapshot of a regional inference latency and transactional failure window, plus a 'self-serve recovery kit' customers can use to minimize downstream impact and verify recovery.
status_page_update: Resolved: Between 2029-12-30T02:40Z and 2029-12-30T05:20Z some requests to the Redwood inference endpoint experienced elevated latency and a small percentage of failures in the us-west-2 region. We have implemented routing fallbacks and request queue smoothing. Most customers should see normal service; please follow the recovery steps below if you continue to experience errors.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a concise, actionable customer update plus a lightweight self-serve toolkit for engineering teams integrating with Redwood APIs. It is intended to be shared directly with enterprise contacts and embedded into a status page update if needed.

Scope and impact:
- Affected scope: Hosted inference endpoints in us-west-2 only; Dedicated and Private deployments not affected.
- Surface area: Text generation and streaming responses (chat) were most impacted. Embeddings and non-streaming batch endpoints had negligible error rate increases.
- Customer impact: ~0.7% elevated error rate (HTTP 5xx) and 4–7x latency spike for requests >1024 tokens during peak of the window. Some streaming sessions were truncated.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2029-12-30T02:22 — First anomalous alerts from tracing and real-user telemetry.
- 2029-12-30T02:40 — Incident declared; initial customer-facing status page entry published.
- 2029-12-30T03:15 — Deployed emergency routing change to shift new traffic to canary routing pool.
- 2029-12-30T04:05 — Implemented queue smoothing and KV-cache warmup heuristics for the main pool.
- 2029-12-30T04:20 — Streaming truncation mitigation enabled (graceful reconnect hints to clients).
- 2029-12-30T05:20 — Monitoring shows error rates return to baseline and latency normalizing; status page updated to "Resolved".

Root cause (high level):
A combination of an unexpected spike in long-sequence streaming requests and a recently deployed memory-sharing optimization caused transient KV-cache thrashing on a subset of serving nodes. The thrash increased p99 latency and caused some streaming sessions to close mid-response. The underlying optimization itself is correct, but under this particular traffic pattern the cache eviction strategy didn't prioritize long-lived KV entries, leading to repeated recomputation.

Actions taken by Redwood engineering:
- Rolled back the cache eviction tweak on affected pools to the prior version.
- Shifted new traffic to a warmed canary pool and increased the canary size by 30% while keeping latency SLOs.
- Deployed a hotfix that prioritizes long-sequence streaming KV entries for eviction lifetime heuristics.
- Added additional telemetry to detect early KV-cache churn for long-sequence workloads.
- Initiated an expanded regression test that simulates a higher proportion of long-stream sessions with variable interleaving.

Customer-facing mitigations and recommended quick actions (self-serve):
If you saw errors or truncated streaming responses during the window, the following lightweight steps will often restore normal operation for your service without waiting for a support ticket: 
1) Retry with jitter: Reissue the request with exponential backoff + jitter. Example: initial delay 250ms, factor 2, max 2s.
2) Prefer non-streaming for long responses: For requests expected to return >1500 tokens, consider using the non-streaming generation API with a higher timeout to avoid transient stream reattachments.
3) Shorten max_tokens or use chunked prompts: Break very long prompts into multiple calls where feasible.
4) Add the routing-preference header to prefer multi-region fallback when available: X-Redwood-Routing: prefer=multi-region.
   - Sample curl to prefer fallbacks:
     curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Redwood-Routing: prefer=multi-region' -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-2.1","prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'
5) For streaming clients: implement graceful reconnect with resume token if you receive a truncated stream; retry the last 100 tokens on reconnect to avoid duplication.

Verification checklist (for customers):
- Confirm your traffic is routing to non-us-west regions: check response header X-Redwood-Region in responses (should be eu-west-1 or us-east-1 when preferring multi-region).
- Check 5xx rate for your tenant between 2029-12-30T02:00Z and 2029-12-30T06:00Z; if >1% please escalate.
- For streaming: validate that session reattaches within 5s on retry; if you see repeated truncation, collect the request_id and timestamps and attach to the ticket.

How we will prevent recurrence (planned next steps):
- Permanent fix: launch revised eviction policy and an automated traffic-shaping rule that caps concurrent long-sequence streams per node.
- Observability: add a KV-churn alert and a long-sequence session heatmap to Console dashboards.
- Testing: integrate long-session stress tests into predeploy pipeline and add continuous chaos trials for memory-pressure scenarios.

SLA and credits:
- Impact window is being assessed against committed SLAs. If your account meets the SLA credit eligibility criteria, a pro-rated credit will be offered automatically. If you need a manual review, include your tenant id and peak error evidence and we will expedite.

Template customer note (editable):
Hi <CustomerName>,
We detected a regional service disruption impacting inference latency and streaming responses in us-west-2 on 2029-12-30. We resolved the issue by rolling back a cache eviction change and deploying targeted mitigations. If you continue to see issues, please follow the recovery steps included here or open a support ticket with incident INC-2029-8472 and your tenant id.

What to attach to a support ticket (if you escalate):
- tenant id
- example request_id (from response headers)
- approximate local time of observed failure
- a description of the operation (streaming vs non-streaming, approx token lengths)

Contacts & escalation:
- Primary CS rep: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- Engineering on-call: oncall-eng@redwood.ai (include INC-2029-8472 in the subject)
- For urgent enterprise SLA review: enterprise-ops@redwood.ai

Notes for internal use (short):
- Follow-up postmortem scheduled 2029-12-31 16:00 UTC.
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Diego Hernández).
- Next internal action: finalize regression test and schedule a canary expansion next week.

Document history and versioning:
- v0.1 2029-12-30 initial incident snapshot (Aisha).
- v0.2 2029-12-31 added self-serve kit and verification checklist (collab: Marcus, Ruth).

End of doc.
recommended_statuspage_snippet: Resolved — region: us-west-2. Root cause: KV-cache churn under long-sequence streaming load. Action: rollback + routing fallback. Affected customers: hosted API in us-west-2. If you continue to see issues, follow our self-serve recovery kit or open a ticket (INC-2029-8472).
